In most places, a landlord is REQUIRED to give proper notice (usually 24-48 hours) before entering your unit, and a blanket email to an entire building does NOT count as proper notice to YOUR specific apartment. Him walking into your friend's room while she was SLEEPING is a massive violation and honestly could be considered illegal entry depending on where you live.

Good on you for having your family friend in law look over the lease! I'd also strongly suggest looking up your state/province's tenant rights laws because I have a feeling your landlord knows exactly what he's doing and is banking on the fact that you're young students who don't know your rights.

Your roommates calling it "covering his ass" is giving him WAY too much credit. A blanket email saying "I might show up sometime" is not proper notice. Period.

Document EVERYTHING. Every email he sends, every time he shows up unannounced, everything. If he continues this behaviour after you've made it clear you know your rights, you may have more options than you think.

So glad the update worked out the way it did! Please do look over that lease carefully and know your rights going forward 😊

Your fiancée is grieving. She's pregnant, far from her family, and the baby shower she grew up imagining - the big NY party with her people around her - is not the baby shower she's getting. That's a real loss and it's hitting her hard. The decorations and the peacock chair and the balloon arch are her trying to salvage something that feels meaningful to her when the thing she actually wants (her family, her culture, her version of this milestone) isn't available to her.

That said - you're not wrong in your assessment of the situation. She didn't want a shower. Then she wanted one but not your mom's version. Then you two took over completely and put real time and money into making it hers. And it still isn't what she wants - because what she actually wants was never really about the decorations at all.

"Ungrateful" was probably not the word to use, and I'd apologize for that specific word. But the underlying frustration you were expressing was legitimate.

What she needs to hear from you is that you SEE what's actually upsetting her - not the balloon arch, but the distance from her family and her culture. Acknowledge that loss directly. Then gently have an honest conversation about what is actually achievable here and what you two can do to include her family in some way, even virtually.

You're both stressed. You're on one income with a baby coming. Give each other some grace.
